regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% is the headline; the quality check is IIP at 6.7% — down from 8.8% prior — with core sector slipping to 5.4% from 6.0%. The composite PMI at 54.6 (83rd percentile) flatters: manufacturing sub-index fell to 52.8 while services carried the composite higher, which means the growth acceleration is services-led and therefore less employment-intensive than the headline suggests. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps — is the one number that genuinely supports private capex optimism, but it needs to clear 80% before boardrooms convert utilisation into committed investment.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"CPI at 4.45% is above the RBI's 4% midpoint, but the real alarm is in the decomposition: fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile, highest in the dataset) is embedding cost pressure across every supply chain that moves goods by road or rail. Core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile) is the apparent comfort — but WPI at 9.92% running 550bps above CPI means producer margins are being squeezed now and retail prices will follow with a one-to-two quarter lag. Invert the consensus read: the market is treating low core CPI as a green light for rate cuts; the correct read is that WPI-CPI divergence of this magnitude historically precedes a core CPI re-acceleration, not a benign plateau.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — is the structural fault line. CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile) has eased one month from 82.5% but remains structurally elevated; the last time India sustained CD ratios above 80% through a rate-cut cycle was FY14, and within four quarters the system faced a deposit rate war that compressed NIMs by 40-60bps across mid-sized banks. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding pressure is migrating upstream — the entities least able to mobilise retail deposits are growing fastest, which is precisely the setup that precedes macro-prudential intervention via risk-weight circulars.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with CPI at 4.45% leaves a real rate of approximately 80bps — thin but positive, and the RBI's own inflation forecast just jumped 50bps to 5.1%, which arithmetically implies the real rate is already negative on a forward basis. An extended pause is the stated stance, but the incentive structure points toward tightening: fuel inflation at a decade high, WPI accelerating, and INR at a 91st-percentile 96.15 all argue for defending the currency through rate credibility rather than through reserve drawdown. The RBI is holding the line with one hand while the data is quietly pushing it toward the door.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the most credible capex signal in two years — commercial vehicle sales at +16.88% and two-wheeler sales at +19.7% confirm that goods movement is accelerating, which is a leading indicator of industrial investment, not a lagging one. Core sector at 5.4% — down from 6.0% — is the one discordant note: cement and steel dispatch growth is decelerating even as capital goods output rises, which suggests the current capex wave is equipment-heavy (machinery, electronics) rather than construction-heavy. That distinction matters for employment multipliers and for which sectors benefit.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore — up 14.8% from ₹1,74,116 crore prior month — is a strong number, but April advance filings and year-end compliance bunching routinely inflate September GST prints; the YTD figure at ₹10,42,757 crore sitting at only the 14th percentile is the corrective. Passenger vehicle sales at +16% and two-wheelers at +19.7% are the cleaner consumption signal — two-wheeler growth at this pace reflects rural income recovery, not just urban discretionary strength, which is a qualitatively different and more durable demand base. Credit card growth at 2.3% (down from 5.6%) is the inversion: if urban consumption were genuinely broad-based, revolving credit would be accelerating, not decelerating — the affluent are spending on vehicles and travel, but mass-market discretionary is more fragile than the GST headline implies.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated at 75th percentile). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% prior, signalling wholesale funding pressure migrating upstream.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% and retail deposit franchises (HDFC Bank, Kotak); underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities and smaller PSU banks dependent on government deposits. RBI will likely signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rate ceilings, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months. Credit growth will moderate unless deposit mobilisation accelerates.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either RBI easing or credit slowdown. Last time CD ratio breached 82% (2022), RBI cut CRR by 50bps within 6 weeks.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firmly Underway, Broadening","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps from 75.6% prior month, at 74th percentile). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% but still positive). GST collections at ₹199,853 Cr YoY (+14.8% from ₹174,116 Cr prior month, 71st percentile). Vehicle sales (CV +16.88%, 2W +19.7%) confirm capex-linked demand.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Kirloskar, Bharat Heavy Electricals), cement (Ultratech, Shree Cement), and steel (Tata Steel, JSW Steel). Capacity utilisation at 77.4% leaves 200-250bps headroom before capex urgency peaks — expect 12-18 month runway. Avoid consumer discretionary; allocate to B2B infrastructure plays and industrial equipment.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at 74th percentile; historically, sustained >76% CU preceded 18-24 months of capex acceleration. Last cycle (2014-2018), CU peaked at 78% before moderating.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Momentum Accelerates, AUM Surges","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (up from ₹31,961 Cr prior month, rising 2 consecutive months, 92nd percentile). SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (up from ₹18.21 Tr, rising 2 consecutive months, 93rd percentile). MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (up from ₹85.76 Tr, rising 2 consecutive months, 86th percentile). SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (up from 99.06 Cr, 82nd percentile). DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months).","implication":"Retail equity inflows are at cyclical highs. Reduce exposure to small-cap and thematic funds; rotate to quality large-caps and dividend-paying stocks.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile; last time SIP inflows were this elevated (2021), they peaked 3-4 months later before moderating 15-20%. DII equity net at 100th percentile is a late-cycle signal.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% prior month, 95th percentile — highest in dataset). WPI at 9.92% (up from 9.78%, 67th percentile). Brent crude at $99.29/bbl (down from $103.87 but still elevated, 70th percentile). WTI at $96.08 (down from $100.30 but 80th percentile). Copper at $6.6915/lb (up from $6.615, 80th percentile, rising 4 of last 5 months).","implication":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a margin compression signal for refiners, airlines, logistics, and power utilities. Underweight Indigo, SpiceJet, and transport stocks. Overweight integrated oil majors (ONGC, Reliance) for hedging. Monitor RBI's next inflation forecast (currently 5.1%, up from 4.6%) — if it breaches 5.5%, expect rate hike signals by Q2 2026. Commodity-linked inflation is the primary tail risk to growth.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a 10-year extreme. Last time fuel inflation exceeded 22% (2022), it persisted for 8-10 months and forced RBI to hike rates 190bps.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"US Rates Sticky, BOJ Tightening Divergence Widens","data_text":"Fed funds rate flat at 3.63% (67th percentile, no near-term cut signals). US 10Y Treasury at 4.94% (down from 5.01%, but 89th percentile — historically elevated). BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile — strongest tightening in G3). Fed balance sheet at $6,746.5B (rising 3 consecutive months, 47th percentile). US core CPI at 2.45% (falling 2 consecutive months, 47th percentile).","implication":"BOJ tightening (1.0% vs Fed 3.63%) is creating a 260bps carry trade unwind risk. Yen strength will pressure India's FII flows and rupee. US 10Y at 4.94% (89th percentile) is a ceiling for global rates — any move above 5.1% will trigger EM outflows. Reduce leverage; hedge INR exposure; avoid high-beta EM plays. Overweight USD-denominated assets and US equities (S&P 500 at 100th percentile, Nasdaq at 72nd percentile).","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 89th percentile is a 10-year high. BOJ at 1.0% is the highest since 2016; last time BOJ tightened this aggressively, yen rallied 15% in 6 months, triggering EM volatility.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"Rupee Weakening Accelerates, Reserves Pressure Builds","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.88, 91st percentile — rising 3 of last 5 months). India VIX at 11.39 (down from 11.39, 6th percentile — complacency signal). FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (up from ₹20,200 Cr, 83rd percentile, but volatile: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631 over 3 months). US VIX at 14.81 (8th percentile — global risk appetite suppressed). DXY at 100.215 (flat, 51st percentile but structurally elevated).","implication":"Rupee at 96.15 is testing 96.5 support; breach will trigger RBI intervention and potential reserve drawdown. India VIX at 6th percentile suggests complacency; expect volatility spike if rupee breaches 96.5. Hedge INR exposure; reduce FII-dependent sectors (IT, pharma); overweight domestic-focused sectors (banks, FMCG, real estate).","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR/USD at 91st percentile is a 10-year weak level. Last time rupee weakened this sharply (2022-2023), RBI intervened with $40B in reserves and raised rates 190bps over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Decouple From IT Stock Weakness","data_text":"Bengaluru office rent at ₹163/sqft (up from ₹148, 95th percentile, rising 3 of last 5 months). Mumbai office rent at ₹171/sqft (up from ₹159, 68th percentile, rising 3 of last 5 months). Office absorption at 26.9 Mn sqft (up from 24.1, 21st percentile — lowest in dataset). Nifty IT index flat at 23,346 (75th percentile, up 3 of last 5 months but no momentum). Office vacancy at 14.5% (down from 15.2%, 42nd percentile). Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (down from 11.6%, 35th percentile).","implication":"Office rents are rising despite IT sector stagnation — this signals GCC (Global Capability Centers) and non-IT corporates (fintech, consulting, manufacturing) are the marginal buyers, not traditional IT services. This is a late-cycle signal: affluent corporates are locking in long-term leases before rates rise further. Overweight commercial real estate (Embassy REIT, Mindspace REIT) and office-focused developers (Prestige Estates, Salarpuria Sattva). Underweight pure-play IT services (TCS, Infosys) — their office footprint is contracting while rents rise, compressing margins. This divergence will persist 12-18 months as GCCs consolidate and IT services rationalize.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Bengaluru office rent at 95th percentile while office absorption is at 21st percentile is a rare divergence. Historically, this pattern preceded 18-24 months of commercial RE outperformance vs IT stocks (2015-2017 cycle).","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a composite PMI of 54.6 (83rd percentile) looks like an economy in full stride — until IIP at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) reveal that the acceleration is narrowing, not broadening. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps — is the genuine bright spot, crossing the threshold where private capex conversations move from boardroom to balance sheet. Against this, fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile) and WPI at 9.92% running 550bps above CPI are embedding cost pressure that will surface in corporate margins within two quarters. Two-wheeler sales at +19.7% and CV sales at +16.88% confirm rural and logistics demand is real — but credit card growth slowing to 2.3% from 5.6% signals that mass-market urban discretionary is softer than the vehicle numbers suggest.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

S&P 500 at 7,650 (100th percentile) with US PMI composite at 56 (84th percentile) is pricing a soft landing with near-certainty — yet US GDP SAAR has decelerated to 1.5% from 2.1%, and US 10Y at 4.94% (89th percentile) is simultaneously pricing a no-cut Fed through year-end. Copper at $6.69/lb rising for four of the last five months (80th percentile) is the commodity market's vote for a global capex upcycle — consistent with iron ore at $161.91 — but China's composite PMI at 49.5 and GDP at 4.3% (down from 5.0%) means the industrial demand signal is coming from the US and India, not from the world's largest commodity consumer. BOJ at 1.0% (86th percentile) tightening while the Fed holds at 3.63% is unwinding the yen carry trade structurally — every basis point of BOJ normalisation repatriates Japanese capital that has been funding EM risk assets for a decade.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore (100th percentile, rising two consecutive months) is the dominant domestic liquidity fact — SIP inflows at ₹32,297 crore (92nd percentile) with SIP AUM crossing ₹18.62 trillion (93rd percentile) means the systematic bid is structurally larger than any single month of FII volatility. FII equity net at ₹29,631 crore is positive but the three-month sequence — ₹-114 crore → ₹-3,112 crore → ₹+29,631 crore — is a reversal, not a trend, and US 10Y at 4.94% with no Fed cut in sight limits how durable that reversal can be. Bank CD ratio at 81.4% with deposit growth at 10.8% against credit at 17.1% means the banking system's internal liquidity is being consumed faster than it is being replenished — the equity market's SIP-driven buoyancy coexists with a credit system running on an increasingly thin deposit base. India VIX at 11.39 (6th percentile) signals complacency that is historically a precursor to repricing, not a confirmation of stability.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 56,359 (93rd percentile) is pricing a credit upcycle — but CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% is the setup for a risk-weight circular, not a re-rating; the last time this configuration appeared, NIM compression followed within three quarters. Office REITs tell a different story: Embassy at ₹369.92 and Mindspace at ₹345.06 are both down sharply from prior levels despite Bengaluru rents at a 95th-percentile ₹163/sqft and Mumbai at ₹171/sqft — the market is discounting that absorption at 26.9 mn sqft (21st percentile) cannot sustain rent levels that have decoupled from occupancy fundamentals. Residential real estate launches at 106,000 units (0th percentile) and sales at 90,715 units (0th percentile) with unsold inventory at 616,000 units confirm that the housing cycle is in a digestion phase — home loan rates at 8.35% rising from a trough of 7.4% are doing the work that affordability math predicted. Gold at $4,424/oz (76th percentile) rising four of the last five months is the hedge that sophisticated money is running alongside the equity long.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact: first, fuel inflation at 22.93% with Brent at $99.29 — every $10 sustained above $90 adds approximately $15bn to India's import bill, widens CAD by 40bps, and feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag at a moment when the RBI's own forecast has already jumped to 5.1%. Second, the CD ratio at 81.4% with NBFC credit accelerating — if deposit mobilisation does not close the 630bps gap within two quarters, the regulator's response will be macro-prudential tightening (risk weights, LCR buffers) that hits credit availability faster than a rate hike would. Third, BOJ normalisation at 1.0% combined with US 10Y at 4.94% is structurally repricing EM carry — INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) with India VIX at a complacent 6th percentile means the currency is vulnerable to a disorderly move if FII equity flows reverse again, as they did as recently as two months ago. Watch Thursday's US core PCE print — at 3.34% it remains the single data point most likely to determine whether the Fed's extended pause becomes a tightening, and every basis point of upside surprise lands directly on the INR.

"}
